Interpreted (CPython), dynamic typing → slower for CPU-bound tasks. GIL restricts thread parallelism. Fast for I/O-bound via async. C extensions (NumPy) for performance.
Transpiles to JavaScript. Performance similar to JS. Node.js (V8 engine) is JIT-compiled, fast for many tasks, especially I/O. Type system helps optimize, but runtime is JS.
JIT-compiled (V8, SpiderMonkey, etc.) → Can be very fast. Single-threaded event loop good for I/O. CPU-bound tasks can block; use Web Workers/worker_threads.
JVM (JIT compilation) → Excellent performance after warmup. Mature GCs. Strong for large, long-running applications. Virtual Threads improve I/O-bound scalability.
Compiled to native code. No GC (ownership model). Zero-cost abstractions. Excellent performance, memory safety. Predictable. Comparable to C/C++.
Compiled to native code. Efficient GC. Lightweight goroutines. Excellent for concurrent network services and CLI tools. Good performance, fast compilation.
Compiled to native code. Manual memory management. Direct memory access. Potential for highest performance but requires careful coding to avoid errors and manage memory.
Compiled to native code. RAII & smart pointers manage memory. Rich features, zero-cost abstractions (if used well). Potential for highest performance.
